components.name: button
components.title: Button
components.purpose: An action the reader takes on the current view.
whenToUse: To start, save, confirm or cancel something on the current view.
whenNotToUse: To go to another view or another site. Use a link.
For an action repeated on every row of a list. Give that one secondary or quiet emphasis, never primary.
As a second primary action in the same view. A view has one.

variants.name: secondary
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Any action that is not the main one.

variants.name: primary
variants.use: The one main action of a view, dialog or popover.

variants.name: quiet
variants.use: A minor action that should not draw the eye, such as Cancel or View log.

variants.name: danger
variants.use: An action that deletes or cannot be undone. The label names what is lost.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall. Use it unless the button sits in a dense row.

sizes.name: small
sizes.use: Drawn 32px tall for dense rows and toolbars. Its pointer target is still 44px.

accessibility: Use a button element, with type="button" unless it submits a form.
The label is a verb and what it acts on, such as Start task. An icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".
Set the disabled attribute when the action is unavailable. A disabled button leaves the tab order.
Use aria-disabled="true" instead only when the button must stay focusable so its reason can be read. The app then ignores presses.
Set aria-busy="true" while the action runs, change the label to say what is happening, and ignore further presses.
Enter and Space activate it. Both come from the button element.

examples.title: Variants
examples.markup:
<button type="button" class="gw-button gw-button--primary">Start task</button>
<button type="button" class="gw-button">Save draft</button>
<button type="button" class="gw-button gw-button--quiet">View log</button>
<button type="button" class="gw-button gw-button--danger">Delete workspace</button>

examples.title: Default and small
examples.markup:

<button type="button" class="gw-button gw-button--small">Copy path</button>
<button type="button" class="gw-button gw-button--quiet gw-button--small">Dismiss</button>

<button type="button" class="gw-button">
  <svg class="gw-button__icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="icons.svg#gw-icon-git-branch"></use></svg>

<button type="button" class="gw-button gw-button--quiet gw-button--small">

components.name: field
components.title: Field
components.purpose: One labelled text input, with its description and its error message.
whenToUse: For one line of text the reader types: a name, a path, a branch, a search term.
Whenever a text input needs a label, which is always.
whenNotToUse: For a choice from a fixed list. Use a select, radio group or checkbox.
For a value the reader cannot change and never needs to copy. Write it as plain text.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The control is 44px tall and as wide as the field. Limit the width on the field's container.

accessibility: Every control has a label element whose for attribute matches the control's id. A placeholder is not a label.
Mark a required control with the required attribute and the word required in the label. Never use colour or an asterisk alone.
Link the description, and the error while there is one, by listing their ids in aria-describedby on the control.
For an invalid value, set aria-invalid="true" on the control and add the error element. Remove both when the value is fixed.
The error message says how to fix the value. Its icon is drawn by the stylesheet, so it needs no markup.
A read-only control stays focusable and its text can be copied. A disabled one leaves the tab order.

examples.title: Label, control and description
examples.reason: The label stays above the control while the reader types, and the description says what a valid value looks like before they start.
